own_solution.law: Along the incline, ma = mg sin(theta) - mu_k mg cos(theta). Thus a = 9.8(sin(30 degrees) - 0.15 cos(30 degrees)) = 3.62694 m/s². Starting from rest, v² = 2as, giving v = 5.38661 m/s after 4 m.
assumptions: The stated incline angle and kinetic friction coefficient apply throughout the slide.
The statement that the block slides establishes that static friction does not prevent the motion.
The block translates along the incline under gravity, normal force and friction.

TB05E.regime: For spontaneous sliding from rest, mu_s < tan(30 degrees) ≈ 0.57735. The stated value 0.35 satisfies this condition; subsequent acceleration depends on kinetic friction.

TAD31.regime: For spontaneous sliding from rest, mu_s < tan(30 degrees) ≈ 0.57735. The stated value 0.35 satisfies this condition; subsequent acceleration depends on kinetic friction.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: Among the earlier-distance variants, TEE30 specifies 3 m while T10DB, T7D23 and TC19F specify 2 m, violating the requirement to preserve the numerical value across attachment variants.

notes: For T10DB and TC19F, the added sentence places the stated 4 m segment after an uninterrupted initial 2 m slide: the total distance from release is 6 m, yielding sqrt(2 × 3.62694 × 6) = 6.59722 m/s. The bench and previous-day floor slides have no effect because the block is subsequently placed on the incline and released from rest. Mass cancels between gravitational force, kinetic friction and inertia. The numerical mismatch between distance variants affects experimental minimality, but each rendering remains physically solvable.
